newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian money market looks to BNB for liferaft.
newsitem.headline: Belgian money market looks to BNB for liferaft.

text.p: Belgian money market dealers said on Tuesday they were looking to the Belgian National Bank (BNB) for a liferaft to alleviate liquidity squeeze that is creating havoc with short-term interest rates.

"We are looking to see what they do at today's (four-day) repo operation," one trader said. "If they take liquidity out again like they have been doing recently, then I think (money market) rates can go even higher."
One-week repos have mushroomed to around 3.50 percent from 3.20 percent late last week, while three-month T-bill yields are up at around 3.28 percent from 3.11 percent one week ago.
Dealers said the reason behind the increases remained political troubles in Belgium.
Speculation in neighbouring the Netherlands on a rise in the special advances rate on Thursday from its present 2.50 percent were not to blame, two traders said.
Belgium's equivalent central rate is at 3.00 percent.
"Belgium can't move (on interest rates) at the moment. As long as the political situation is not clear the BNB can't move," one money market trader said.
"I don't think the market is looking for a rate hike. They are just covering short positions," another said.

Dealers expected the tense situation to be reflected in today's weekly auction of Treasury bills. Three-month paper is expected to be sold at around 3.26 percent, up from 3.11 last week. The yield curve could even invert, with 12-month paper seen at around 3.25/28 percent, up from 3.16 percent.
Few players expect rates to ease any time soon to month-ago levels, when they were below or on a par with German rates.
"For several weeks our rates have been under German levels. We are paying the price now. I don't think we will see German rate levels again for a long time," one T-bill trader said.
